Triggers.value: Night-time or waking up in the dark

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I drink alcohol, take medication or use drugs

vignette: Kaius had always been drawn to the creative field, and his work as a graphic designer allowed him to express himself in ways that brought him joy. But it was on a fateful night two years ago, during a routine traffic stop, that his life took a drastic turn. The police officer's tone had shifted from courteous to aggressive in an instant, and Kaius found himself face-to-face with the barrel of a gun. The sound of screeching tires still echoed in his mind as he recalled the officer's words: "You're going down for this." Though charges were eventually dropped, the encounter left an indelible mark on Kaius. In the weeks that followed, Kaius began to notice a creeping sense of unease that seemed to seep into every aspect of his life. Nighttime, once a time for rest and rejuvenation, now felt like a descent into darkness. He would wake up in a cold sweat, his heart racing, as the shadows on his wall seemed to twist and writhe like living things. The sound of sirens or the sight of cars similar to the one he had been driving that night could send him spiraling into a panic. Crowded places, once energizing, now felt suffocating – the crush of bodies and the cacophony of noise threatening to overwhelm him at every turn. As these triggers began to exert their hold on his life, Kaius found himself increasingly reliant on maladaptive coping strategies. He would drink to excess, hoping to dull the edges of his anxiety, or take medication to calm the racing thoughts that plagued him. But it was the sight of police uniforms or weapons that sent him into a tailspin – he would cover his face with his hands, as if to shield himself from the memories that threatened to resurface. Even at work, where creativity and imagination had once flowed freely, Kaius now found himself avoiding projects that involved military or law enforcement themes. As the months dragged on, these avoidance behaviors began to take a toll on his relationships and career. His ex-wife, tired of his increasing isolation and erratic behavior, eventually left him. Colleagues at work grew concerned about his declining productivity and increased absences. And yet, Kaius couldn't seem to break free from the cycle that had taken hold – every trigger seemed to lead him down a rabbit hole of substance use and avoidance. It was only when he found himself unable to attend his niece's birthday party, held in a crowded park on a sunny afternoon, that Kaius realized the depth of his struggles. He had been too afraid to face the crowds, too anxious about the possibility of seeing police officers in attendance. The shame and regret that followed were a wake-up call – he knew he needed help to break free from this cycle of avoidance and substance use. As he sat in his dimly lit apartment, the shadows cast by the fading light outside seeming to mock him, Kaius finally felt ready to confront the demons that had haunted him for so long.
